questions.question_text: Which of the following errors will not affect the agreement of the Trial Balance?
options: D) Wrong posting to a ledger account
questions.answer: A) Error of complete omission

questions.question_text: Wages paid for the installation of a new machinery is debited to the Wages Account. What type of error is this?
questions.answer: C) Error of Principle

questions.question_text: A Suspense Account is generally used to rectify errors occurring at which stage?
options: A) Before the preparation of Trial Balance
B) After the preparation of Trial Balance
C) After the preparation of Final Accounts
D) During the preparation of Cash Book
questions.answer: B) After the preparation of Trial Balance

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the main cause of depreciation?
options: D) Rise in general price level
questions.answer: B) Normal wear and tear

questions.question_text: Under the Written Down Value method, the amount of depreciation:
questions.answer: C) Decreases every year

questions.question_text: A provision is created to meet:
options: B) A known liability, the amount of which cannot be determined with substantial accuracy
C) A known liability, the amount of which is exactly known
questions.answer: B) A known liability, the amount of which cannot be determined with substantial accuracy

questions.question_text: Which reserve is created out of capital profits and cannot be distributed as cash dividends?
questions.answer: C) Capital Reserve

questions.question_text: If Closing Stock appears inside the Trial Balance, where will it be recorded in the Final Accounts?
options: B) Profit and Loss Account only
D) Both Trading Account and Balance Sheet
questions.answer: C) Balance Sheet only

questions.question_text: Outstanding wages are classified as which type of account?
questions.answer: C) Representative Personal Account

questions.question_text: Accrued income is an income that has been:
questions.answer: B) Earned but not received

questions.question_text: Which formula correctly represents Cost of Goods Sold?
options: A) Opening Stock + Purchases - Closing Stock
B) Opening Stock + Purchases + Direct Expenses - Closing Stock
D) Both B and C are correct
questions.answer: D) Both B and C are correct

questions.question_text: Prepaid Insurance given in the adjustments is treated by:
options: A) Adding to insurance in P&L and showing on Liabilities side
B) Deducting from insurance in P&L and showing on Assets side
C) Deducting from insurance in P&L only
D) Adding to insurance in P&L and showing on Assets side
questions.answer: B) Deducting from insurance in P&L and showing on Assets side

questions.question_text: Goods distributed as free samples should be credited to which account?
questions.answer: C) Purchases Account

questions.question_text: Bad debts recovered during the year are transferred to:
options: B) Profit and Loss Account (Credit Side)
D) Provision for Bad Debts Account
questions.answer: B) Profit and Loss Account (Credit Side)

questions.question_text: Under the Single Entry System, if Closing Capital is greater than Opening Capital, the difference indicates:
options: A) Profit for the year (assuming no drawings or additional capital)
questions.answer: A) Profit for the year (assuming no drawings or additional capital)

questions.question_text: To find out the credit sales under the Single Entry System, which account is prepared?
questions.answer: C) Total Debtors Account

questions.question_text: What is a Statement of Affairs?
options: A) It is another name for a Trial Balance
B) It is an exact replica of the Profit and Loss Account
C) It is a statement of assets and liabilities to find capital balances
D) It is a Cash Flow statement
questions.answer: C) It is a statement of assets and liabilities to find capital balances

questions.question_text: Which of the following is considered a revenue expenditure?
options: B) Paying annual road tax for the delivery van
C) Constructing an extension to the warehouse
D) Installing a new air conditioning unit
questions.answer: B) Paying annual road tax for the delivery van

questions.question_text: In a manufacturing business, carriage inward is recorded in the:
questions.answer: C) Trading Account

questions.question_text: When closing stock is overvalued, the current year's net profit will be:
questions.answer: B) Overvalued

questions.question_text: Define the purpose of a Suspense Account in the rectification of errors process. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A suspense account temporarily holds the difference in a trial balance until one-sided errors are located and rectified, ensuring final accounts can be prepared without delay.

questions.question_text: Explain the underlying logic of the Written Down Value (WDV) method of depreciation. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The WDV method applies a fixed percentage to the asset's declining book value each year, matching higher repair costs in later years with lower depreciation charges.

questions.question_text: State the primary difference between a Provision and a Reserve. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A provision is a charge against profit created for known, estimated liabilities. A reserve is an appropriation of profit created to strengthen the business's overall financial position.

questions.question_text: How is an outstanding salary expense treated in the final accounts? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Outstanding salary is added to the salaries expense on the debit side of the Profit and Loss Account and shown as a current liability in the Balance Sheet.

questions.question_text: Identify the accounting treatment for goods withdrawn by the proprietor for personal use. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Goods withdrawn are debited to the Drawings Account and credited to the Purchases Account, effectively reducing the cost of goods available for sale in the Trading Account.

questions.question_text: What is the primary objective of preparing a Statement of Affairs in incomplete records? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The primary objective is to determine the opening or closing capital balances by listing and deducting total liabilities from total assets on a specific date.

questions.question_text: Pass a rectification journal entry: Furniture purchased for $5,000 was debited to the Purchases Account. Assume the Trial Balance is already closed. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Debit the Furniture Account by $5,000 to record the asset properly, and credit the Purchases Account by $5,000 to cancel the incorrect expense entry. This rectifies the error of principle completely.

questions.question_text: Sales Book is undercast by $1,500. Pass the rectifying entry assuming a Suspense Account has been opened. Describe the effect. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Debit the Suspense Account by $1,500 and credit the Sales Account by $1,500. This action correctly increases total sales revenue while clearing the unexplained discrepancy temporarily held in the Suspense Account.

questions.question_text: Calculate depreciation for a machine purchased on July 1, 2025, for $40,000. The rate is 10% p.a. on the Straight Line basis. Books close March 31, 2026. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The annual depreciation is 10% of $40,000, which equals $4,000. Because the machine was used for 9 months (July to March), the proportional depreciation is calculated as $4,000 multiplied by 9/12, yielding $3,000.

questions.question_text: A firm's Debtors balance is $52,000. Bad debts in adjustments are $2,000. Create a 5% Provision for Doubtful Debts. Show the P&L and Balance Sheet impact. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Subtract $2,000 from $52,000 for good debtors ($50,000). The 5% provision equals $2,500. In P&L, debit $4,500 total ($2,000 + $2,500). In the Balance Sheet, show Debtors at $47,500 ($50,000 less $2,500).

questions.question_text: Calculate a manager's commission of 10% on net profit after charging such commission. The net profit before the commission is $22,000. Show the formula calculation. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The formula is Net Profit Before Commission multiplied by (Rate / (100 + Rate)). Therefore, $22,000 multiplied by (10 / 110) yields a manager's commission of exactly $2,000.

questions.question_text: Outline the journal adjustment for prepaid insurance of $1,200 found outside the Trial Balance, and explain its placement in the financial statements. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Debit Prepaid Insurance and credit the Insurance Expense Account by $1,200. In the statements, deduct $1,200 from Insurance in the P&L debit side, and report $1,200 as a current asset on the Balance Sheet.

questions.question_text: Determine the Cost of Goods Sold given: Opening Stock $10,000, Purchases $40,000, Carriage Inwards $2,000, Sales $65,000, and Closing Stock $15,000. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Cost of Goods Sold equals Opening Stock plus Purchases plus Direct Expenses minus Closing Stock. Calculation: $10,000 + $40,000 + $2,000 = $52,000. Subtracting the $15,000 closing stock yields a COGS of $37,000.

questions.question_text: Ascertain Opening Capital: Closing Capital is $80,000, Drawings during the year are $15,000, Additional Capital introduced is $10,000, and the year's Net Profit is $20,000. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Start with Closing Capital ($80,000), add Drawings ($15,000) making $95,000. Then deduct Additional Capital ($10,000) and Net Profit ($20,000). The resulting Opening Capital calculated is $65,000.

sections.section_name: Section D - Long Answer (LA) / Problem Solving

questions.question_text: Draft a Trading and P&L Account structure with adjustments. Trial Balance items: Purchases $80,000, Wages $10,000, Rent $5,000. Adjustments: Outstanding Wages $2,000, Prepaid Rent $1,000, Closing Stock $12,000. Detail the step-by-step placements. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: In the Trading Account debit side, list Purchases at $80,000. Show Wages at $10,000, add $2,000 outstanding for a $12,000 total. Credit Closing Stock at $12,000. In the P&L debit side, list Rent at $5,000, subtract $1,000 prepaid, extending $4,000 to the outer column. Show outstanding wages as liability and prepaid rent and closing stock as assets.

questions.question_text: A business bought Machinery for $100,000 on April 1, 2023. It charges 10% p.a. depreciation under the Written Down Value method. Determine the book value of the machinery on March 31, 2026, showing the calculation schedule for three full financial years. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Year 1 depreciation is 10% of $100,000 = $10,000. Book value on April 1, 2024 is $90,000. Year 2 depreciation is 10% of $90,000 = $9,000. Book value on April 1, 2025 is $81,000. Year 3 depreciation is 10% of $81,000 = $8,100. The final book value on March 31, 2026, equals $72,900.

questions.question_text: Provide rectifying entries and the Suspense Account balance for these errors: (a) Goods sold to Ram for $2,000 were posted as $200. (b) Rent paid $1,500 was completely omitted from the ledger. (c) Purchase returns book overcast by $400. Assume the difference in TB was originally placed in suspense. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: For (a), debit Ram and credit Suspense by $1,800 to fix the under-posting. For (b), debit Rent and credit Cash by $1,500 (no suspense). For (c), debit Purchase Returns and credit Suspense by $400. The Suspense Account absorbs these one-sided corrections, revealing an initial credit difference of $2,200 in the trial balance.

questions.question_text: Convert single entry incomplete records to find total sales. Debtors on April 1: $12,000. Debtors on March 31: $18,000. Cash received from debtors during the year: $45,000. Discount allowed to debtors: $1,000. Bad debts written off: $2,000. Cash sales are $20,000. Describe the calculation matrix. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Prepare a Total Debtors Account. On the credit side, aggregate Cash Received ($45,000) + Discount Allowed ($1,000) + Bad Debts ($2,000) + Closing Debtors ($18,000) = $66,000 total credits. Subtract Opening Debtors ($12,000 debit) to find credit sales of $54,000. Add Cash Sales ($20,000) to credit sales. The total sales for the period equal $74,000.
